author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Three Florida Gators named to College Sports Communicators Academic All-America teams
text:
Three members of the Florida Men’s Swimming and Diving team were recognized on Apr. 29 for their academic and athletic achievements during the 2025-26 season, earning College Sports Communicators (CSC) Academic All-America honors.
The recognition highlights the importance of balancing academic success with athletic performance at the collegiate level. The CSC Academic All-America program celebrates student-athletes who excel both in their sport and in the classroom.
Leading the group, Liendo was named CSC Academic All-America Division I Men’s Swimming and Diving Team Member of the Year and earned a spot on the Academic All-America First Team. This marks his second consecutive selection to the first team, making him only the fourth Gator swimmer to receive multiple CSC Academic All-America honors alongside Brad Deborder, Greg Reeves, and Kevin Nead. Liendo graduated with a degree in Education Sciences and maintained a cumulative grade-point average of 3.56. In his senior season, he was recognized as a seven-time First Team All-American at the NCAA Division I National Championships, bringing his career total to 26 such honors. He also became just the second Gator in program history to sweep his individual events (50 free, 100 free, and 100 fly), joining Caleb Dressel in that achievement.
Joining Liendo on this year’s First Team is Brown, who earned his degree in Computer Science with a GPA of 3.89 while graduating cum laude. Brown received Second Team All-American status for his performance in the 1,650-freestyle event at nationals.
Gesing rounds out Florida’s honorees as part of the Second Team. The junior diver holds a GPA of 3.86 while majoring in Education Sciences and achieved top finishes at nationals by placing fifth in three-meter diving and sixth on one-meter board—earning First Team All-American status for both events.
Florida student-athletes have now received this honor 178 times overall across all sports; men’s swimming and diving athletes account for twenty-three CSC Academic All-America recognitions within that total.
